Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Titas Sadhu to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Bangladesh Women have a job to do. Their bowlers were sloppy at times. The fielding was yet again below par, dropping around 3 catches and allowing some freebies to flow away as well but they bowled well in patches. Mind you they are still in game. This is a chaseable target but batting has been the weakness for the home team in this tour and yet again they'll depend on their top three or maybe top four to give them a rollicking start. Can they chase it down?

A decent recovery from Bangladesh Women as at one stage they were ready to concede more than 180 runs. However, they struck in consecutive deliveries to get rid of Harmanpreet Kaur and Dayalan Hemalatha who were going hard from both ends. India were all set for a big score, thanks to the start from Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. They both fell but Kaur and Dayalan Hemalatha made sure the intent didn't drop. Both lost their wickets at crucial time but Ghosh's cameo means they still have a competitive total on the board.
Dot to end the over! Flat and outside off, Sharma looks to cut but misses. India Women finish with 156 for 5.

TOSS - India Women have won the toss and will BAT.

It is time for the fifth and final match between Bangladesh Women and India Women. The series was decided way long back, India Women have taken an unassailable lead of 4-0 and are looking for clean sweep. Bangladesh Women on the other hand have failed to produce a decent performance once in the series and are on the brink of whitewash at home. Nigar Sultana will hope her team show some intent in this match and avoid a clean sweep while India will hope a couple of their batters get some runs under their belt and the bowlers keep up the good work. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.
...MATCH DAY...

The Indian women's cricket team is on the verge of achieving a clean sweep as they gear up to face Bangladesh in the fifth and final T20 International of the series, amidst a backdrop of weather disruptions in Sylhet. With a dominant display in the previous encounters, India aims to maintain their unbeaten streak and conclude the series on a high note. Despite weather interruptions affecting two matches, India's bowlers have showcased exceptional prowess, consistently stifling the Bangladesh batting lineup. However, the same cannot be said for their batting performance, with only one fifty-plus score recorded across four matches, courtesy of Shafali Verma's impressive knock of 51 in the series opener. The lack of substantial contributions from key batters like Smriti Mandhana and captain Harmanpreet Kaur highlights the team's batting concerns, especially considering the upcoming women's T20 World Cup to be hosted by Bangladesh later this year. As they approach the final encounter, Mandhana and Kaur will be eager to seize the opportunity to make significant contributions with the bat. With Mandhana's elegant strokeplay and Kaur's aggressive approach, India will look to bolster their batting lineup and post a formidable total against Bangladesh. The duo's ability to capitalize on scoring opportunities and play impactful innings will be crucial in ensuring India's dominance and securing a comprehensive victory. With pride at stake and momentum on their side, India will be determined to deliver a commanding performance in the final T20I, reinforcing their status as a formidable force in women's cricket. As the spotlight shines on Sylhet, all eyes will be on India as they strive to clinch a convincing win and complete a memorable whitewash against Bangladesh.
